speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (a) what are the Government's key considerations in deciding to tighten regulations for digital payment token service providers, including the prohibition of payments via locally issued credit cards; and (b) what is the anticipated impact on younger consumers, particularly those aged 18 to 25, who are increasingly adopting the use of cryptocurrencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: More generally, using credit or leverage magnifies losses and investors can lose more than the principal amount they put in.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What is MAS' view on banning cryptocurrencies and will it lead to consumers going underground?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And given that individuals aged 18 to 25 are increasingly adopting cryptocurrencies, what specific factors did the Ministry consider regarding this demographic when formulating these regulations?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And how does the Ministry plan to address these unique financial literacy and risk exposure challenges faced by younger consumers?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I will start with the second one, and that is, the Government will continue to step up communications to warn consumers of all ages on the hazardous nature and the highly risky, volatile nature of cryptocurrencies.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And that does not just apply to the youths, but it also applies to any consumer who deals with cryptocurrencies.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: On the broader perspective of what MAS' views are on cryptocurrency, MAS seeks to foster an innovative and responsible digital asset ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: But this is very different, and there is a sharp distinction that we need to draw between growing an innovative and responsible digital asset ecosystem, and the distinction between that and speculation in cryptocurrency, which MAS has consistently discouraged to the retail public.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And so, such a prohibition may be unlikely to be effective in limiting its harms.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Therefore, to reduce the risk to consumers from speculative trading in cryptocurrencies, MAS requires that digital payment token service providers ensure proper business conduct and provide adequate risk disclosures.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In fact, these regulatory measures are comprehensive to reduce consumer harm in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: They include consumer access provisions, business conduct provisions, as well as technology risk provisions.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: But our message is clear, it is consistent: consumers should steer clear of cryptocurrencies.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Assoc Prof James Lim, a short supplementary question to give the Minister of State time to answer.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I had filed a crypto-related question yesterday about holdings by our Sovereign Wealth Funds (SWFs).

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I am wondering if I could follow-up a little little bit on that.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I fully agree with the Minister of State that for the retail investor, there are substantial risks.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But I think there is an evolving understanding of the role of cryptocurrencies as a balancing asset, much like gold.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: And while I do not take any position about the utility of it in our SWF portfolios, I am wondering if MAS has a view about what it means for institutional investors, whether at the SWF level or institutional investors in the Singapore financial ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I think that that question has been answered yesterday as a written Parliamentary Question, about that position.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I also wanted to clarify with the Member what is his, and as well as the party's position, on cryptocurrency in general.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Assoc Prof Lim, do you want to respond?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Sure, I am happy to explain that for me, I do not hold any inherent favour or not.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: But I would like to understand what cryptocurrency means for institutional investors, much like how we draw a distinction between encouraging retail investors with a certain kinds of asset investments, as opposed to institutional investors.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And so, they invest in assets that are anchored to underlying economic fundamentals with the potential for long-term value increase.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
